candidates.tagline: Honda CR-V wipers can't reach the whole windshield — 'it's a feature, not a bug'
candidates.story: The 2023–2026 Honda CR-V places windshield-washer nozzles on the wiper arms instead of the hood, so coverage is poor — and owners report the driver-side wiper doesn't sweep the full windshield up to the A-pillar; when taken to dealers, they were told it is 'a feature, not a bug.'
candidates.why_funny: Honda engineered four consecutive model years of a rain-clearing system that can't fully clear the rain, and the official position is that this is working as intended.
candidates.alt: 2023 Honda CR-V EX-L AWD in white photographed from the front-right, the exact model affected by the wiper-arm nozzle design that leaves the A-pillar corner unwiped

candidates.tagline: Ring's answer to 'too many cameras outside' was an AI drone inside your house
candidates.story: On November 10, 2026, Amazon's Ring — already under fire for letting police access doorbell footage without warrants — launched Ring Robotics: a $270 'Ring Drone Cam' that autonomously flies room-to-room inside your home when an alarm trips, and a $1,000 'Ring Rover Cam' that rolls through your office on a patrol schedule.
candidates.why_funny: Ring's entire PR problem has been 'we gave your outdoor footage to the police' — their fix was to launch an AI drone that follows you around inside your own house.
candidates.alt: The Ring Drone Cam, a compact white quadcopter indoor security drone shown docked in its charging station — Ring's new autonomous flying camera that patrols the inside of your home
